title: Adapting Career Ideas
text: Being able to reflect on and change career ideas and the strategies used to achieve them.
cdi_links: 4.C.03 Being able to reflect on and change their career ideas and the strategies that they are pursuing to achieve them

title: Introduction
bullets: Career plans are not fixed and may shift as you learn more about yourself and the world of work
Explore how careers and job roles can evolve over time
Reflect on your current career ideas and assess their fit with your interests and goals
Identify strategies to adapt your plans and revise your career plan when needed

title: Success Criteria
bullets: I can reflect on my current career ideas
I can describe how careers and job roles can change over time
I can explain what adaptability means in the context of careers
I can identify ways to adjust my plans if my interests or circumstances change
I can revise my career plan and outline alternative strategies

title: Key Words
bullets: Career Evolution – How jobs, industries, and career paths develop and change over time
Strategy – A plan of action designed to help you reach a goal or achieve an outcome
Career Adaptation – Adjusting your ideas, strategies, and plans as your interests or the world around you changes

title: Starter Activity
bullets: Has your career idea changed since Year 7? If so, why?
Why do some jobs disappear while new ones are created?
What careers exist today that did not exist 10 years ago?

title: How Careers Change Over Time
bullets: The world of work evolves due to technology, new industries, and global events
New roles emerge while some jobs fade away (e.g., social media managers, green energy roles)
Understanding these changes helps you make informed career decisions

title: Career Adaptability
bullets: Career adaptability is the ability to adjust your career ideas, strategies, and plans when needed
Includes being open-minded, staying informed about labour market changes, and developing transferable skills
Trying alternative pathways and being willing to learn new things increases long-term career control

title: Reflecting on Your Current Ideas
bullets: Your interests, strengths, and goals may change over time
Reflecting helps determine if your plan still fits who you are and what you want to become
Key questions: What do I enjoy now? What am I good at? Have my priorities changed? What new opportunities have I discovered?

title: Alternative Strategies
bullets: Explore different routes such as apprenticeships, college, or T-levels
Focus on transferable skills like communication or problem-solving
Seek advice from employers or mentors, adjust your timeline, or try taster sessions and work experience
Being flexible keeps your career options open

title: Activity – Reflect and Adapt Your Career Plan
text: Reflect on your current career ideas and consider how they might evolve. Practice adapting your plan by exploring alternative pathways and strategies. Include: your current career interest, why it appeals to you, relevant skills or experiences, possible changes to your plan if circumstances or interests change, and strategies to stay on track.

title: Adapting Career Ideas
sentence: Successful careers often require people to stay ______ and adjust their ______ when opportunities or interests change.

title: Key Takeaways
bullets: Reflecting on your career ideas and being adaptable helps you respond to changing opportunities
Using alternative strategies and flexible planning increases control over your long-term career success
